html:
In 1826 King Anouvong of Vientiane rose against Siam, which had ruled the Lao kingdoms since 1779. His armies marched deep into the Khorat plateau before being driven back.

Siam's answer was harsh. In 1827 and 1828 its troops sacked and razed Vientiane, leaving only a few temples such as Wat Si Saket standing. Anouvong was caught and died in captivity in Bangkok.

Tens of thousands of Lao were moved across the Mekong to the Khorat plateau, which is why Isan, northeast Thailand, now has more Lao speakers than Laos itself. Thais remember the war as a victory; Lao remember Anouvong as a hero. See the split of Lan Xang and French Laos.
